# 6. Discussion

[[OUTLINE ¶1. state the puzzle before addressing it. Agricultural service delivery is expected to widen the set of technologies a farmer can reach. On these estimates it does not appear to: communities with a service source sit on a frontier further below the meta-frontier, not closer to it, while their farmers use that frontier better. Give both figures once. Numbers: objs$eff$services0$tgr$gap and objs$eff$services0$te$gap. Close the paragraph on the fact that the two nearly cancel (objs$eff$services0$mte$gap), because the rest of the section is about why that cancellation should not be read as an absence of effect.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶2. set out the readings of a negative technology gap, without yet choosing. Three are available. (a) Placement: services are directed toward communities whose accessible technology is already behind, so the sign of the association is not the sign of the effect. Section 4.4 concedes this cannot be ruled out on these data and names it the sharpest unobserved confounder. (b) A real constraint: extension and farmer organisations propagate a standardised package that sits below the best technology available to the most capable producers, so exposure compresses the technology set rather than expanding it. (c) A composition effect: the served group is nearly twice the size of the unserved group and more heterogeneous, and a group frontier fitted over a wider population sits further from an envelope defined by the best performers anywhere. Reading (b) is the only one that makes the estimate a genuine effect of services, and it is the one requiring the strongest evidence.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶3. THE PIVOT OF THE SECTION. Three pieces of internal evidence discriminate, and all three point away from reading (b).

     First and strongest, service content does not move the technology gap. Across the four service types estimable on the served side, the technology component varies from about −0.05 to −0.09 while the efficiency component varies from +0.41 to −0.31. If the negative gap were something services do, changing what a service menu contains should move it; it barely does. Numbers: objs$by_service$services_post_harvest$provided$tgr and $services_mechanization$provided$tgr for the narrow range, the matching $te fields for the wide one.

     Second, the gap closes across the period, to an estimate indistinguishable from zero by 2016/17, while the efficiency gap does not move. A constraint imposed by services should not dissolve while the services expand. A placement pattern should attenuate as coverage widens and targeting becomes less selective, which is what Section 2.1 shows happening beneath a flat headline share. Numbers: objs$by_wave$tgr$gap by round, and objs$by_wave$te$gap alongside.

     Third, the gap is largest exactly where the served group is most selected. Associations show a technology gap difference roughly three times the aggregate, and Section 2.2 found association communities distinguished chiefly by schooling rather than by scale or input use. Numbers: objs$eff$services1$tgr$gap against objs$eff$services0$tgr$gap.

     State the conclusion at the strength the evidence carries, which is that reading (a) is the most economical account and reading (b) is not supported, not that placement has been demonstrated. The design cannot separate them and Section 4.4 says so.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶4. the contrast. Put the efficiency gap through the same three tests and note that it behaves differently on every one. It varies with service content in a way the technology gap does not. It is stable across rounds where the technology gap collapses. It is positive under both extension and associations, and the one source where it is not is also the one where neither component is individually significant. A component that responds to what services do, when they are delivered, and how, is the component that behaves like a treatment effect. This is the paper's substantive finding and the paragraph should say so plainly.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶5. what follows for the net measure. Meta-technical efficiency is the product of a placement-contaminated component and an informative one, so its near-zero value is not evidence that agricultural services do not matter. It is what happens when a selection artefact of one sign is multiplied by a treatment-like effect of the other. Make the methodological point at the level it deserves: a study reporting only overall performance would have recovered a small positive number and concluded very little, and the decomposition is what makes the result legible. This is the strongest general claim the paper has for readers outside Ghana.

     The sign reversal across rounds belongs here rather than in ¶3, because it is a consequence of the decomposition rather than evidence for it. Overall performance runs from negative in 2005/06 to positive in 2016/17, so the pooled figure is an average across a comparison that reverses direction and no single round produces it. Any single-number summary of what agricultural services did in Ghana between 2005 and 2017 is therefore misleading, whichever sign it carries. Numbers: objs$by_wave$mte$gap by round against objs$eff$services0$mte$gap.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶6. the three sources. Extension is the clean case: both components move in the direction the aggregate implies and the net difference is the largest positive of the three. Associations show the same directions at close to three times the magnitude and end up net negative, which ¶3 has already used as evidence of selection and which can be stated here as a substantive difference between institutional forms rather than only as a diagnostic. Cooperatives are the odd case and deserve one honest sentence: neither component is individually distinguishable from zero yet their product is, which is a property of how the two errors covary rather than a finding about cooperatives, and it should not be presented as one. Numbers: the objs$eff$services1, $services2 and $services3 blocks.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶7. service content and where the efficiency gain sits. Post-harvest and marketing support carries by far the largest positive efficiency difference, planting and agrochemical advice smaller positive ones, and mechanization a large negative. Since ¶3 has established that the technology component is near-constant across these, the content result is a statement about utilisation: what a community's service menu contains bears on how well farmers use the frontier available to them and almost not at all on which frontier that is. The mechanization reversal is the one that needs an account rather than a restatement, and it should be given one or explicitly left open. Numbers: the $provided$te fields across the four estimable service types in objs$by_service.]]

[[OUTLINE ¶8. policy, at the level the design supports and no further. What can be said: within a balanced sample, operating in a served community is associated with better use of the available production frontier, that association is strongest where services include post-harvest and marketing support, and it is not visible in overall performance because the technology comparison works against it. What cannot be said: that provision causes these differences, or that individual participation would produce them, since the treatment is community availability and Section 2.1 states that uptake and provision diverge by an amount the data cannot measure. Close on the practical implication of ¶5, which is that programme evaluation resting on a single aggregate performance measure will understate what service delivery does.]]
